subject: Game Theory
title: International Trade Deals
description: A quick, practical guide to International Trade Deals.

hook.text: NAFTA took seven years to negotiate. The TPP involved 12 nations and thousands of trade-offs.

buildup.text: Trade deals are multi-issue, multi-party games. Each country trades concessions on different sectors.

discovery.text: Agriculture vs. manufacturing, IP vs. labor rights—each pair of issues creates logrolling opportunities.

twist.text: Domestic politics complicate everything. Negotiators must satisfy their own voters while appeasing trade partners.

climax.text: Putnam's 'two-level game' theory shows negotiators play simultaneously at the international and domestic tables.

punchline.text: Every trade deal is really two negotiations.

quiz.question: What is Putnam's 'two-level game' theory?
options: Negotiators must satisfy international and domestic audiences simultaneously
